Plot categorization decision functions and response boundaries

Source: R/S7-generics.R, R/S7-plot-methods.R
plot_categorization_functions.Rd

Visualizes predicted categorization response probabilities and decision boundaries across cue dimensions for cognitive models and fitted Stan models. Supports proportional probability matching, deterministic criterion/MAP classification, and stochastic sampling decision rules, fully accounting for perceptual noise and lapses.

Usage

plot_categorization_functions(
  x,
  cues = NULL,
  categories = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  aes = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  decision_rule = "proportional",
  resolution = 100,
  noise_treatment = NULL,
  lapse_treatment = NULL,
  ...
)

## S7 method for class <MVBU_CognitiveModel>
plot_categorization_functions(
  x,
  cues = NULL,
  categories = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  aes = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  decision_rule = "proportional",
  resolution = 100,
  noise_treatment = NULL,
  lapse_treatment = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An MVBU object (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation, MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate, MVBU_CognitiveModel, or MVBU_Stanfit).

cues

Character vector of cue names to plot (1, 2, or 3 cues). Defaults to all cues of the model up to 3 (or the first 3 cues if the model has more than 3 cues, analytically marginalizing out all remaining dimensions). At most 3 cue dimensions can be plotted simultaneously.

categories

Character vector of category names to evaluate and plot. Defaults to the first category (get_category_labels(x)[1L]).

groups

Character vector of group names to plot. Defaults to NULL (all groups).

aes

Plot aesthetic: "contour", "fill", "fill-gradient", or "fill-discrete". Defaults to "contour" for 1D/2D static plots, and "fill-discrete" for 2D interactive plots (interactive = TRUE). When interactive = TRUE (or aes = "interactive"), renders a 3D response probability surface via Plotly.

levels

Numeric vector specifying response probability contour levels. Defaults to c(0.01, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.99).

limits

Optional named list or numeric vector specifying axis / cue limits (e.g. list(F1 = c(200, 800), F2 = c(800, 2500))). Defaults to NULL (automatically computed from category distributions or exemplars).

decision_rule

Character string specifying the decision rule to use for categorization predictions ("proportional", "criterion", or "sampling"). Defaults to "proportional".

resolution

Integer specifying grid resolution along continuous cue dimensions. Defaults to 100L for 1D and 60L for 2D/3D.

noise_treatment

Treatment of perceptual noise during evaluation: "no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize". Defaults to NULL (uses the model's configured noise treatment).

lapse_treatment

Optional character string specifying treatment of attentional lapses: "no_lapses", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_lapses": Lapses are ignored; categorization reflects pure normative evidence evaluation (even if lapse_rate > 0).

  • "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses on individual observations. With probability lapse_rate, a lapse occurs and the posterior is replaced by lapse_bias.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities), mixing normative posteriors with lapse_bias: \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\).

Defaults to NULL (uses the model's configured lapse treatment).

...

Additional arguments passed to specific plotting methods:

  • uncertainty_treatment: Treatment of posterior parameter uncertainty in fitted Stan models ("marginalize" or "sample").

  • ndraws: Integer specifying the number of posterior MCMC draws to use from MVBU_Stanfit (defaults to 20L).

  • show_exposure_data, show_test_data: Logical; if TRUE, overlays observed exposure/test data points.

  • parallel, n_cores: Logical and integer controlling parallel grid evaluation.

  • noise_treatment: Optional character string specifying perceptual noise treatment ("no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize").

  • interactive: Logical; if TRUE, produces interactive 3D WebGL scenes via Plotly.

  • slices, slice_cue: Configuration for 3D sliced category plots.

Value

A ggplot object (or a plotly htmlwidget if interactive = TRUE).

See also

plot_categories, plot_parameters, categorize, posterior

Examples

mod <- example_mvg_ideal_observer(n_cues = 2)
plot_categorization_functions(mod)
